full_judgment:
2. The opposite party nos. 1-13 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 29 of 1986. The Court of Subordinate Judge, Jamalpur for declaration of their title in the suit land and recovery of possession in which the petitioner, the Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Jamalpur was impleaded as the defendant No. 3. Their case, in short, is that the suit land measuring 3.36 acres described in the schedule of the plaint originally belonged to Sarat Sundari Chowhurani, who sold the same to Dijendra Lal Roy by a registered deed of sale dated 19.12.1917; that Dijendra Lal Roy possessed the suit land on payment of rent; that his name was recorded in the S.A. Khatian as the owner of the land; that he gifted the land to her daughter Uma Rani Roy by a registered deed of gift dated 11.3.1970; that while Uma Rani Roy was in possession of the land through bargadars transferred the same to the plaintiff nos. 1 and 2 by a registered deed of sale dated 21.8.1973; that the plaintiff no. 1 transferred some portion of the suit land to other plaintiffs by different kabalas of different dates; that the defendant No. 1 claiming himself as the owner of the suit land on the basis of lease allegedly taken by him from Mohini Mohan Chowdhury filed O.C. Suit No. 74 of 1974 in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Jamalpur for declaration of his title challenging enlistment of the suit land as vested property, which was dismissed; that the defendant no. 1 managed to get the suit land enlisted as vested property and threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs therefrom; that then the plaintiffs filed O.C. Suit No. 64 of 1984 for permanent injunction, during pendency of which the plaintiffs were dispossessed from the suit land on 20.4.1984 and thereafter they filed the present suit for recovery of the possession after establishment of their title in the suit land. 

 8. Admittedly the suit land originally belonged to Sarat Sundari Chowdhurani. It is also admitted that the suit land was recorded in the name of Dijendra Lal Roy in S.A. Khatian. According to the plaintiff, Dijendra Lal Roy purchased the suit land from the original owner. Sarat Sundari, by a registered deed of sale dated 19.12.1917 A.D. That deed is Exbt. 2. The defendant no. 1 and the defendant no. 3, (the present petitioner), challenged the genuineness of that deed. According to them it is forged and recent creation taking the advantage of gutting the record room of Mymensingh District Registrar's record room that the original owner Sarat Sundari Chowdhurani did not transfer the land to Dijendra Lal Roy; that she died leaving her adopted son Mohini Mohan Chowdhury who inherited the suit land and migrated to India. Further case of the defendant no. 1 that Mohini Mohan Chowdhury before leaving the country leased out the suit land to his father and thus his father became owner of the suit land which was inherited by him. On the other hand the case of the defendant no. 3 (petitioner) is that as Mohini Mohan Chowdhury, the owner of the suit land migrated to India after partition of India, the suit land by operation of land vested to the Government as vested property.
